overall.sentence: The closest earlier work, the same group's bilayer-graphene interferometer at half filling (2412.19886, cited as [18]), shares system and method; what is new is the gate-defined antidot that selects whether the e/2 interfering anyon braids around a localized e/2 (pi jump) or e/4 (pi/2 jump), for which no earlier precedent was found in the paper's references and 10 arXiv searches (2026-11-22).

assessment.claim: 1: gate-tunable FPI in bilayer graphene with an embedded antidot controls the number and type of localized anyons
assessment.note: Ghosh et al. ([19]) already placed a gate-defined antidot inside a GaAs FQH interferometer to introduce localized quasiparticles; question and method match, the bilayer-graphene platform and even-denominator selectivity are new.

assessment.claim: 2: pi phase jumps at nu = -1/2 from e/2 encircling one more localized e/2; such sharp jumps 'have not been reported before' at nu = -1/2
assessment.note: An et al. (2011) and Willett et al. (2019) reported discrete pi phase slips in GaAs interferometers at nu = 5/2, a half-filled Landau level; neither is cited. New here: bilayer graphene, antidot control, and the e/2-e/2 assignment.

assessment.claim: 3: pi/2 phase jumps from e/2 encircling a localized e/4, expected non-Abelian
assessment.note: No precedent found in the paper's references and 10 arXiv searches (2026-11-22): earlier GaAs 5/2 work saw e/4 interference, even-odd alternation and pi flips, but not a pi/2 e/2-around-e/4 braiding jump; only the method (FPI) matches.

assessment.claim: 4: time-resolved switching resolving individual anyon tunnelling events into the loop
assessment.note: Werkmeister et al. ([12]) resolved real-time telegraph switching of anyon number in a graphene FPI at nu = 1/3 and 4/3; new here is the antidot-controlled setting and the even-denominator filling.

positioning: The paper builds on the same group's bilayer-graphene interferometer at half filling (2412.19886) and on real-time telegraph braiding at nu = 1/3 in graphene (2403.18983, 2403.19628); its addition is an antidot that selects the localized anyon type, giving pi and pi/2 jumps at nu = -1/2. The searches found no earlier report of a pi/2 e/2-around-e/4 jump, but the GaAs nu = 5/2 interference literature (Willett et al. 2009, 2019; An et al. 2011), which reported e/4 and e/2 interference, even-odd alternation and discrete pi phase slips, is not cited and is the natural point of comparison. A concurrent bilayer-graphene antidot interferometer paper (2603.11182) reports controlled localization of e/4 at half filling; it was posted after this paper and is context only.

issues.claim: Sharp aperiodic phase jumps at nu = -1/2 have not been reported before.
issues.headline: Earlier GaAs 5/2 phase slips not cited beside the priority statement
issues.issue: The sentence claims sharp aperiodic jumps at nu = -1/2 are unreported. Literally true for bilayer graphene, but An et al. (arXiv:1112.3400) and Willett et al. (arXiv:1905.10248) reported discrete, roughly pi phase slips in GaAs interferometers at nu = 5/2, also a half-filled Landau level, and neither is cited. A referee from that community will ask how these jumps compare.

edit.before: In contrast, the aperiodic jumps are sharply defined and, in the case of ν = −1/2, have not been reported before.
edit.after: In contrast, the aperiodic jumps are sharply defined; at ν = −1/2 in bilayer graphene they have not been reported before, while phase slips of about π were reported in GaAs interferometers at ν = 5/2 [An et al. 2011; Willett et al. 2019].

issues.claim: Selective braiding of e/2 with localized e/2 or e/4 anyons at an even-denominator state.
issues.headline: Introduction omits GaAs 5/2 interference with e/4 and e/2
issues.issue: The introduction summarises even-denominator interference only through refs. 18 and 19, but Willett et al. (arXiv:0911.0345, arXiv:1905.10248) reported e/4 and e/2 interference at nu = 5/2 with an even-odd alternation attributed to the number of enclosed e/4 anyons. That is the same question, interference sensitive to localized e/4 number, in another system, and should be weighed against the paper's selectivity result.

evidence.quote: In contrast, experiments in hole-conjugate and even-denominator states reported interference of anyons whose charge followed the filling factor.

issues.fix: Add a sentence on the GaAs nu = 5/2 interference work and state that this paper differs by gate-selecting the localized anyon type and resolving individual pi and pi/2 jumps in time.

edit.before: In contrast, experiments in hole-conjugate and even-denominator states reported interference of anyons whose charge followed the filling factor.
edit.after: In contrast, experiments in hole-conjugate and even-denominator states reported interference of anyons whose charge followed the filling factor. Earlier GaAs interferometers at ν = 5/2 reported alternating e/4 and e/2 oscillations and π phase flips attributed to the number of enclosed e/4 anyons [Willett et al. 2009, 2019], without control over the localized anyon type.

prior.overlap: FPI at nu = 5/2 where interference depends on the parity of enclosed localized e/4 quasiparticles.
